To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the human gut microbiome is shaped by breast-feeding and that human milk oligosacchrides (HMOs) are the main drivers of this shaping.

the consumption of HMO by the infant microbiota is a key factor in the establishment of the infant gut ecosystem and that this consumption can lead to the production of short chain fatty acids that can have an impact on host physiology.
the consumption of HMO by Bifidobacteria and Bacteroidetes is mediated by the presence of specific enzymes, which are encoded by the genomes of the bacteria and are not present in the human host.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of HMO in infant gut microbiota and their impact in infant health.
the role of HMO in the establishment and maintenance of the infant gut microbial community and its potential impact on infant health.
the role of HMO in the development of the intestinal microbiome, and with the role of the intestinal microbiota in the metabolism of these complex carbohydrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

HMO are not only substrates for the growth of Bifidobacteria and Bacteroidetes but also for other members of the infant intestinal microbiome, such as Lactobacillus, Clostridium, and Faecalibacterium.

the consumption of human milk oligosacchardies by Bifidobacteria is a highly efficient process that can be considered as an important source of nutrients for these bacteria in the gut of the breast-fed infant.
the infant gut is a complex system where HMOs play multiple roles in the development of the microbiome, and in the health of the infant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HMO are not simply consumed by the gut microbiota, but are rather a major source of nutrients for the intestinal microbiota.
Bifidobacteria are able to consume HMO, but only after the HMO have been cleaved by a specific glycosidase, while Bacteroides are able to cleave and consume HMO.
HMO are a major source of nutrition to the infant microbiota.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consumption of HMO by Bacteroides is not as straightforward as previously thought and is dependent on a number of factors.

the HMO composition of human milk can have an important impact on infant gut microbiota, and that HMO consumption may play an important role in the establishment of the bifidobacterium-dominated microbiota of breastfed infants.
HMO are consumed by the infant intestinal microbiome and that the consumption of specific HMO can be used to drive the growth of specific members of the microbiome.
